concepts.title: Posets, Hasse diagrams, chains & antichains
concepts.blurb: A partial order is a reflexive, antisymmetric, transitive relation; its Hasse diagram is the transitive reduction. Chains are totally ordered subsets, antichains are mutually incomparable ones, and their extremes give the height and width of the poset.

concepts.title: Lattices: meet & join
concepts.blurb: A lattice is a poset in which every pair has a meet (greatest lower bound) and a join (least upper bound). Distributive and modular lattices are pinned down by the forbidden sublattices M3 and N5.

concepts.title: Dilworth's theorem
concepts.blurb: In any finite poset the size of a largest antichain equals the minimum number of chains needed to cover it. Mirsky's dual swaps the roles: the longest chain equals the minimum number of antichains covering the poset.

concepts.title: Sperner & the Boolean lattice
concepts.blurb: The Boolean lattice B_n of subsets ordered by inclusion has its largest antichain at the middle layer, of size C(n, floor(n/2)). This is Sperner's theorem, proved by the LYM inequality.

concepts.title: Möbius functions & inversion
concepts.blurb: Every locally finite poset carries a Möbius function defined by mu(x,x)=1 and mu(x,y) = -sum over x<=z<y of mu(x,z). Möbius inversion generalizes inclusion-exclusion (on the Boolean lattice) and classical number-theoretic Möbius inversion (on the divisor lattice).

concepts.title: Complete lattices & Knaster–Tarski
concepts.blurb: A complete lattice has meets and joins of arbitrary subsets. Knaster–Tarski: any monotone map on a complete lattice has a complete lattice of fixed points, with a least fixed point equal to the meet of all pre-fixed points.
